classification.difficultyReason: Combine two isosceles triangles with the exterior angle theorem to simplify algebraic angle expressions.

inlines.text: , for all the angles in this triangle.
(Hint: simplify the expressions as you go)

spec.description: Unshaded triangle XWZ with Y on the horizontal base XZ and internal segment WY. Single ticks identify WX = XY; double ticks identify WY = YZ. The angle at X is labelled 2x without a degree symbol.
spec.mathematics: X, Y and Z are collinear in that order. WX = XY and WY = YZ create two isosceles triangles. Angle WYZ is exterior to triangle XWY.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated angle expressions appear.

answer.short: $\angle XWY=\angle XYW=90-x$; $\angle WYZ=90+x$; $\angle YWZ=\angle WZY=45-\frac{x}{2}$. The whole triangle has $\angle WXZ=2x$, $\angle XWZ=135-\frac{3x}{2}$ and $\angle WZX=45-\frac{x}{2}$.
answer.worked:
Since $WX=XY$, the base angles of $\triangle XWY$ are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle XWY=\angle XYW&=\frac{180-2x}{2}\\&=90-x\end{aligned}$$
By the exterior angle theorem in $\triangle XWY$,
$$\begin{aligned}\angle WYZ&=2x+(90-x)\\&=90+x\end{aligned}$$
Since $WY=YZ$, the base angles of $\triangle WYZ$ are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle YWZ=\angle WZY&=\frac{180-(90+x)}{2}\\&=45-\frac{x}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Adding the adjacent angles at $W$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}\angle XWZ&=(90-x)+\left(45-\frac{x}{2}\right)\\&=135-\frac{3x}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Also, $\angle WXZ=2x$ and $\angle WZX=\angle WZY=45-\frac{x}{2}$.
